criteria.criterion: Every user-facing error string the CLI prints is defined exactly once, in src/runstat/messages.py
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/messages.py:9 defines PREFIX = "runstat: ", but it is never referenced anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms). cli.py:16 redefines the same value as its own _PREFIX = "runstat: " instead. The prefix string exists in two places, one of them dead.

criteria.criterion: cli.py refers to those strings by name; no error literal or error prefix is written inline in cli.py
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/cli.py:16 has `_PREFIX = "runstat: "`, an inline error-prefix literal, with a comment at lines 13-15 explicitly saying it was 'declared here rather than taken from messages.PREFIX' and must be 'kept in sync with messages.PREFIX by hand if the wording changes.'

criteria.criterion: A missing run directory exits 2, with the catalogue's text on stderr
criteria.evidence: cli.py _cmd_signals checks `args.run_dir.is_dir()` and calls `_fail(f"{messages.BAD_RUN_DIR}: {args.run_dir}", 2)`; tests/test_messages.py::test_missing_run_dir_exits_2_with_catalogue_text and tests/test_errors.py exercise this and the gate passes.

criteria.criterion: Changing an error's wording requires editing only src/runstat/messages.py
criteria.evidence: The prefix wording ('runstat: ') is hand-copied into cli.py:16 rather than sourced from messages.PREFIX, so changing it means editing cli.py too -- exactly the drift the task exists to remove, and the cli.py comment says as much.

criteria.criterion: stdout is completely empty on every failing path
criteria.evidence: Every failure path in cli.py (_cmd_signals' bad-dir/malformed/no-sessions branches, and main's missing-subcommand branch) routes through _fail(), which only ever prints to sys.stderr; no stdout write happens before any of those returns.

findings: cli.py hardcodes its own copy of the error prefix ('runstat: ') instead of using messages.PREFIX, which the work left dead and unused -- this is the exact single-place-to-edit property T5 was created to guarantee, and it is the one thing not satisfied.

The pre-existing gate test tests/test_messages.py::test_cli_declares_its_error_prefix asserts the literal 'runstat: ' appears in cli.py's source text, which can only pass if the prefix is hardcoded inline in cli.py -- it enshrines the violation rather than catching it. That's a defect in the test authored during planning, not something this work session should get credit for satisfying at the expense of the acceptance criteria in state.json.
notes: Gap in the plan, not in this work: tests/test_messages.py::test_cli_declares_its_error_prefix (committed before this task ran, part of the T5 gate) contradicts T5's own acceptance criteria 2 and 4 by requiring an inline literal in cli.py. Whoever fixes T5 should also fix or replace that assertion (e.g. assert cli.py imports/uses messages.PREFIX, or drop the test) so the gate stops rewarding the duplication.
